name: Monarch Butterfly Fund Small Grants Program
summary: Small grants from a monarch conservation charity for habitat conservation, monitoring, outreach and sustainable development projects, mainly around the oyamel forests of central Mexico, with limited support in the US and Canada.

geography.label: Central Mexico, with limited US and Canada

amount.note: Renewable for a second year; larger amounts considered case by case

reporting: A final report at the end of the project, plus interim reports whenever activities or planned expenses change.

steps: MBF Board review of complete proposal

eligibility.rule: Research applicant is an advanced undergraduate or graduate from Mexico or at a Mexican university
Has Reserve authority approval for work in or around the Monarch Butterfly Biosphere Reserve
Has affected-party approval for research, community-involved or communal-property projects
Assessment or monitoring directly relates to monarch conservation

documents: Reserve Director approval, if work is in the Reserve
Local community approval, if the work involves local communities
Faculty advisor support letter, if submitted by a student

status.quote: Applications may be submitted at any time.

applicant_types.quote: The Monarch Butterfly Fund welcomes proposals from organizations or individuals

geography.quote: Most of MBF's funding supports activities focused on protecting the oyamel fir forests in which monarch butterflies overwinter as well as their migration in central Mexico.

access.quote: The Monarch Butterfly Fund welcomes proposals from organizations or individuals

amount.quote: For most projects, funding is limited to $3,500 US per year, with the possibility of renewal for a subsequent year.

window.quote: Applications may be submitted at any time.

reporting.quote: In addition to a final report at the completion of the project, interim reports should be submitted by email to grants@monarchconservation.org whenever there are changes in the activities or planned expenses of the project.

effort.quote: Applications may be submitted at any time.
Whenever possible, submissions that are complete are reviewed by the MBF Board at the next scheduled board meeting.

eligibility.quote: Research funds will be available to graduate or advanced undergraduate students who are from Mexico or are studying at a Mexican university.
All projects to be carried out within the Monarch Butterfly Biosphere Reserve and surrounding areas must have the approval of the Reserve's authorities.

If the projects involve research, interaction/participation of local communities (ejidos and indigenous communities) or are in the communal properties, then they must also have approval from the parties involved.
Any proposed assessment or monitoring activities must have direct relevance to monarch conservation.

after_award.quote: In addition to a final report at the completion of the project, interim reports should be submitted by email to grants@monarchconservation.org whenever there are changes in the activities or planned expenses of the project.

documents.quote: A cover page with the title of the proposed project; the strategic initiative(s) that the work addresses; the date of submission; the name, address, and e-mail address (if available) of the person responsible for the work; and the total amount requested. 2. An abstract of 150 words or fewer.

A description of the affiliations and role of each participant in the project in addition to the primary applicant. 4. A summary of previous work by the organization, including, if relevant, websites and names of individuals who are involved with the work of the organization (no more than 1 page).
Description of proposed work ____ Timeline of activities

A detailed budget with justification of proposed expenses (1 page), including funding from other sources and an estimate of what amount will be needed to reach your goals. 7. Approval by groups affected by this proposal. If work is to be accomplished in the Reserve, approval in writing from the Director. If work involves local communities, approval in writing from those affected.
If the proposal is submitted by a student, confirmation in writing of support for the project by the student's faculty advisor.
